election_source.title: Calling control of Congress in the 2026 midterm elections
election_source.note: AP lists all six as winners; race calls are not state certifications.

shared_vote_source.title: Final Vote Results for Roll Call 312
shared_vote_source.note: H.R.9340 passed House 417–3. Barr, Hageman, Hern (OK), Letlow and Moore (AL) all listed among Yeas. Support for this limited ratepayer measure is not opposition to data-center development. Requires consideration of standard, not mandatory adoption.

profiles.name: Harriet Hageman
profiles.classification_note: Verified support for limited ratepayer safeguards and oversight; supports state siting authority. Energy expansion to serve data centers is contextual, insufficient alone for a broad pro-development tag.
profiles.campaign_priority: Discussed in campaign interview; dedicated campaign plank not verified.
profiles.summary: Backs state/local siting review and ratepayer protection; demanded Meta explain water-system contamination in Cheyenne.
proposals: Use Wyoming's Industrial Siting Act for local/state review
Require timely information about water contamination

sources.title: Interview with Harriet Hageman, Republican Party candidate for U.S. Senate
sources.quote: I think that we have the law in place to make sure that our local communities can properly address this issue.
sources.summary: Says data-center siting is a state issue, with sufficient existing Wyoming Industrial Siting Act review.

sources.title: Hageman Demands Answers from Meta Over Data Center Water Contamination
sources.quote: Water is a precious resource in our state
sources.summary: Asked Meta for answers about contamination of Cheyenne's reuse-water system; local utility officials said residential drinking water was not threatened.

profiles.ads: No directly verified data-center campaign ad located in targeted searches.

profiles.name: Andy Barr
profiles.classification_note: Conditional development support and limited ratepayer safeguards. Local-control preference does not establish blanket opposition to regulation.
profiles.campaign_priority: Explicit campaign interview position; dedicated platform plank not verified.
profiles.summary: Argues data centers can deliver jobs and local revenue, with scrutiny, local siting control and protections against electricity cost shifts.
proposals: Leave project approval to local governments
Encourage data centers to bring their own power

sources.title: Barr wants to see regulations, decisions on data centers left up to local governments in KY
sources.quote: my position on all of this is local control, national American leadership in this area.
sources.summary: Describes construction jobs and tax revenues as benefits; says facilities could lower electric rates if supplying their own power; supports scrutiny and local decisions.

profiles.ads: No directly verified data-center campaign ad located in targeted searches.

profiles.name: Kevin Hern
profiles.classification_note: Tag rests on recorded vote for limited ratepayer safeguards, not a verified broad regulatory campaign platform.
profiles.campaign_priority: Dedicated data-center campaign priority not verified.
profiles.summary: Voted for the House's limited ratepayer-protection measure. No original-source direct quote verified in this pass.

sources.title: Final Vote Results for Roll Call 312
sources.summary: Hern (OK) is listed among Yeas on H.R.9340.

followup.note: Oct29 interview reportedly addressed local data-center siting control. Original inaccessible; secondary ChamberLight summary only. Do not present as verified quote.

profiles.ads: No directly verified data-center campaign ad located in targeted searches.

profiles.name: Barry Moore
profiles.classification_note: Supports limited ratepayer safeguards; broad development position not established. Do not confuse with Alabama state Rep. Parker Moore.
profiles.campaign_priority: Official legislative position documented; dedicated Senate campaign plank not verified.
profiles.summary: Supported the House ratepayer bill as a step toward protecting customers as energy demand grows.

sources.title: House passes bill aimed at addressing impact of data centers on energy costs
sources.quote: It’s a good step in the right direction
sources.summary: Moore endorsed the ratepayer bill; all Alabama House members voted for it. Article explains regulators must consider the cost-allocation standard.

profiles.ads: No directly verified data-center campaign ad located in targeted searches.

profiles.name: Julia Letlow
profiles.classification_note: Explicit conditional support for development plus ratepayer safeguards.
profiles.campaign_priority: Explicit official statements during campaign; dedicated campaign plank not verified.
profiles.summary: Supports responsible data-center investment for jobs and local tax benefits, while backing safeguards against shifting electricity costs to households.
proposals: Have large projects pay their own power-related costs

sources.title: Letlow Votes for Ratepayer Protection Act
sources.quote: When developed responsibly, these investments can support our economy by creating new jobs
sources.summary: Supports data-center economic benefits and ratepayer protection. Office describes mandatory adoption more strongly than the bill; use bill text for legal effect.

sources.title: Julia Letlow Discusses Louisiana Economic Growth, Data Centers and Federal Legislation
sources.summary: Presented Meta's Richland Parish development as an example of addressing its energy needs; discussed preventing cost shifts to existing customers.

profiles.ads: No directly verified data-center campaign ad located in targeted searches.

profiles.name: Kurt Alme
profiles.classification_note: Explicit transparency, water, electric-rate and community-consent guardrails. Conditional acceptance alone not coded broad pro-development.
profiles.campaign_priority: Yes: data-center transparency and local decisions appear in campaign website's issue list; interview provides detail.
profiles.summary: Wants transparent costs and impacts, water protection, local jobs, no household electricity increases and community support before development.
proposals: Full disclosure of costs and community impacts
Companies bear their own costs and create local jobs
Protect water users and water quality
Guarantee no increases in household electricity costs

research_limitations: Targeted name+data-center searches, official office/site searches, news and campaign interviews checked. Absence of verified campaign plank/ad is not proof none exists. No anti-regulation category established for these six; local authority arguments do not alone justify it. Alme campaign page supported by search extract with direct-fetch failure. Hern radio original blocked; retain as follow-up only.
